title: Port Pplr from shell scripts to Rust
objective: Replace Pplr's bash scripts, Python helpers and run-time-compiled Swift engine with one Rust binary, `pplr`, that serves every command the shell version offers today with the same arguments and flags, and reads and writes the People tree byte for byte as the legacy code does. It ships no Python. It keeps live Contacts access through a thin Swift I/O sidecar built ahead of time. The existing bats suite, made safe and honest first, proves it on macOS and Linux.
context:
**Why now.** hv wants Pplr as a Rust CLI installed through Homebrew (ST0002). The shell version cannot be: it compiles its Swift engine at run time into the checkout, it needs `PPLR_ROOT`, and its handler bakes in a checkout path. It also ships Python, which the user-scope rules forbid, and its CI has been a false green.

**hv's rulings, 2026-11-02.** The Python goes, all of it. The core is Rust. Swift is acceptable where Contacts needs it, because it is already written. The test suite is to be cleaned up, not trusted.

**What is there** (the attached `recon.md` has the detail):

- bash: the dispatcher and 30 commands, 2,442 lines.
- Swift: a 1,681-line engine that holds the people model, the `pplr://` markers, `resolve`, `links` and all of the Contacts sync logic.
- Python: four helpers (tags, contact cadence, the plan workbook, the email listing), 1,030 lines.
- Tests: 99 black-box bats tests.
- The last CI run reported success with 9 tests failing on macOS and 41 on Ubuntu, because the runner exits with `rm`'s status. The test teardown can also delete whatever an inherited `PPLR_TEST_DATA` names.
- Gtools reads the same People tree through `PPLR_DIR` and `PPLR_DATA`.

**How** (the attached `design.md` has the decisions D1 to D10, the module map and the rules):

- One Rust core, with Contacts behind a store interface: a JSON store for the tests and a Swift sidecar cut down to I/O for the live store.
- A fallback, so the bats suite stays green against the Rust binary at every step, and each command has one live implementation at a time.
- Goldens captured from the legacy code, so every data file stays byte-identical.
- Cldr's house style.
- 13 work packages split between dc (the safety, scaffold, Contacts and doctor groundwork) and cc (the port).

**Inputs.** dc's boot findings and cc's survey, in vc's inbox at 2026-11-02 07:37Z and 07:38Z.

**Related.** ST0002 ships this binary through Homebrew under devbin's dev/opt/brew contract. The install layout is the seam between them: ST0001 WP02 and ST0002 WP01, both dc's.

wps.title: Test safety, the parity seam and an honest runner
wps.objective: Make the bats suite safe to run anywhere, honest about failure, and able to test either implementation. Then record what it says about the legacy code today.
wps.body:
**Scope**

- Each test keeps its data under `$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR`. No path taken from the environment, `PPLR_TEST_DATA` or any other, is ever a deletion target.
- One setting chooses the implementation under test (name it here, eg `PPLR_UNDER_TEST=<path to a pplr executable>`), defaulting to the checkout's `bin/pplr`. `setup()` stops resetting `PPLR_BIN_DIR`.
- `tests/run_tests.sh` exits with bats' status and deletes nothing it did not create. The tests generate the files they need under `tests/fixtures/` (`.cache/email-last.json`, `.mock_bin/claude`, `.mock_home/`) per test, and those files are no longer tracked.
- `.github/workflows/test.yml` fails when a test fails. WP02 replaces this workflow, so keep the fix minimal.
- **Baseline against the legacy code**:
  - on rhadamanth, through the bats lane (`intent estate slots`);
  - on CI, for both runners.
  - Record ok, not ok and skipped per runner on this thread, with a one-line triage per failing test: a legacy defect, an environment gap (eg no `uv` in CI) or a test defect.
  - The last CI run already shows, on macOS, the 7 contact tests, test 21 (`doctor --fix`) and test 33 (`new` directory structure); on Ubuntu, those plus test 41 and every test that needs the Contacts framework.

**Criteria**: AC-01.1 to AC-01.4.

**Not in scope**: fixing the legacy defects the baseline finds. They are triaged, and the port either inherits the test or the triage says why not.

**Hand-off**: cc's WP03 uses this harness, and WP02's gates run the suite through the seam.

wps.title: Rust scaffold under devbin, with the fallback
wps.objective: Stand up the Rust crate in house style, with devbin's gates and CI on macOS and Linux. Build a `pplr` binary that runs every command, natively once ported and through the fallback until then, so the whole bats suite passes against it from this WP on.
wps.body:
**Scope**

- **The crate** (design D5 and 3.1):
  - `Cargo.toml` at the root: package `pplr`, version 2.0.0, edition 2024, `rust-version`. rhadamanth has Homebrew's Rust and no rustup, so there is no `rust-toolchain.toml`. `[lints]` sets `unsafe_code = "forbid"` and denies `unwrap_used` and `expect_used`.
  - `rustfmt.toml` with `edition = "2024"` and `tab_spaces = 2`.
  - A thin `src/main.rs`, plus `src/lib.rs`, `src/cli.rs` (the command table, the argument helpers, help generated from the table), `src/error.rs`, and `src/config.rs` (the data root per D8, the XDG defaults per D5).
  - `tests/cli.rs` with a `Sandbox`, after Ccusage's.
- **The fallback** (design 3.3). This WP ports no command: every command, `version` and `help` included, runs through the fallback until its own WP.
- **devbin**:
  - Make the vendored devbin 0.1.19 (`bin/devbin`, `bin/.devbin/`) ready to commit, with its config declaring `rust`, and `shell` for the suite.
  - `check all` and `test all` run the cargo gates (fmt, clippy with the house lints, test, autotests, targetdir) and the bats suite against the Rust binary, through WP01's seam.
- **Hygiene**: rewrite `.gitignore` for Rust and Swift (`target/`, `tmp/`, `.build/`) and drop the Mix entries; fence `bin/.devbin/lib/` in `.prettierignore`; remove the tracked Finder `Icon\r`.
- **CI**: `.github/workflows/tests.yml` on macOS and Linux, hardened as in ST0002 E6, running the cargo gates and the bats suite against the Rust binary. Retire `test.yml`. ST0002 WP02 adds the `candidate/**` trigger.
- **The install-layout seam** (design 3.4), agreed with ST0002 WP01: one function returns the binary's resolved root and the sidecar's path beside it.
- **Languages**: with hv's agreement, run `intent lang init rust shell swift` so the critic gate arms.

**Criteria**: AC-02.1 and AC-02.2.

**Heavy runs** go through `intent estate slots`: cargo and bats each have one heavy lane, shared with Devbin and Utilz.

**The People leak check** (D11): a check in the gate, eg `bin/devbin check people-leak` called from the pre-commit hook. It reads the folder names, their `pplr://` markers and the About emails from `PPLR_DATA` at run time and fails on any match in the staged tree. The names are never written into the repo. Skip it with a stated reason when `PPLR_DATA` is absent (eg on CI).

**AGENTS.md**: `intent claude upgrade` generated build and test lines for a SwiftPM package (`swift build`, `swift test`, `Package.swift`), but the sidecar is a single file compiled with `swiftc`. Correct them through Intent's generator, never by hand-editing `AGENTS.md`.

wps.objective: Capture the exact output of every command that writes or reports, from the legacy implementation over a synthetic People tree, as goldens the Rust binary must reproduce byte for byte.

wps.title: Core model and the read commands
wps.objective: Build the core every command shares (the tree, person references, the About header, normalisation and markers), and port the commands that only read.
wps.body:
**Scope**

- **Modules** `tree`, `about`, `normalise` and `marker` (design 3.1), as pure functions with unit tests taken from the Swift and bash behaviour:
  - the walk rules;
  - `PersonRef`, which accepts two arguments, `Surname, First`, `L/Surname, First` or a `pplr://` marker;
  - the header fields as the engine reads them;
  - case and diacritic folding matching Swift's on the fixtures, phones, Gmail keys and LinkedIn slugs;
  - the marker path and URL, aliases, and `pplr://tag/<t>`.
- **Native commands**: `resolve`, `count`, `about`, `cp`, `open`, `linkedin`, `edit`, `meetings`, `refresh`, `grep`, `help` and `version`.
  - `open` percent-encodes without `python3`, and probes the CMS without `curl` if that stays simple.
  - The version tests are re-pointed at `Cargo.toml`.
- **Deletion**: rewire any legacy caller first (eg `pplr_open` calls `pplr cp`), then delete these commands' bash.
- **Errors** go to stderr (D10).
- **`edit`** honours `$VISUAL`, then `$EDITOR`, running the editor in the foreground, and refuses naming both when neither is set (D10).

**Criteria**: AC-04.1.

wps.title: Indexes, new person, pictures and search
wps.objective: Port the index builders, person creation, the picture line and search.
wps.body:
**Scope**

- `json`, byte-identical to `jq .`'s print, and `index`.
- `reindex` runs the Rust index builders. Until WP06 lands it runs the legacy `tags render` through the fallback.
- `new`: the git author (`git config user.name`) in the verblock, pinned in the goldens by a sandboxed git config (D10); the embedded template, with `_pplr/templates/person` overriding it; the `.webloc` from its fixed template; the About regenerated when a URL is given.
- `pictures`.
- `search`:
  - runs the `claude` subprocess with the prompt and the index, and parses its reply as JSON;
  - falls back to the keyword search;
  - never interpolates the query into a command line, which fixes the `sed` injection.
- Delete these commands' bash.

**Criteria**: AC-05.1.

wps.title: Tags
wps.objective: Port tags to Rust and retire `tags.py`.
wps.body:
**Scope**

- **Choose the YAML reader by evidence.** It must read every `tags.yaml`, `vocabulary.yaml` and `cadence.yaml` shape the goldens hold the way PyYAML does: dates, YAML 1.1 booleans such as a bare `no`, and flow mappings. Record the choice and its evidence in this WP. `serde_yaml` is deprecated.
- **Subcommands**:
  - `tags check`, `show`, `edit` and `apply`;
  - `tags render`: the Tags line, the `_tags/` pages, and unused pages removed;
  - `tags index`: `tags_index.json` in Python's `indent=1` format;
  - `tag`, which re-renders `(Contact).md` through the fallback until WP07 lands.
- **`tags.yaml`** comes from a port of `tags.py`'s emitter, not from a YAML library.
- Delete `pplr_tags`, `pplr_tag` and `src/pplr-tags/tags.py`.

**Criteria**: AC-06.1.


**The YAML reader: the choice and its evidence** (cc, as built)

- **Chosen: `src/yaml.rs`, a reader of the subset pplr's files use, resolving plain scalars by PyYAML's YAML 1.1 rules.** No dependency.
- **Why not a crate.** The legacy code used every value through Python's `str()` and `json.dumps`, so the reading has to match PyYAML's types, not just its text: a bare `no` is the boolean False and prints `False`, `at: 2026-09-25` is a date that prints as itself, `180` is an int. The maintained Rust readers (`yaml-rust2`, `saphyr`) follow YAML 1.2, where `no` is the string "no", and have no date type; `serde_yaml` is deprecated.
- **What it reads:** block mappings and sequences (a list may share its key's indent, as PyYAML allows), flow mappings and sequences, plain, single- and double-quoted scalars with their escapes, and comments; plain scalars resolve to null, bool (the YAML 1.1 set), int (decimal, `0x`, `0b`, octal, `_` separators), float, date, or string. Block scalars, anchors, tags, reserved indicators and multiple documents are refused with the line named, never misread.
- **Evidence:** every `tags.yaml`, `vocabulary.yaml` and `cadence.yaml` shape in the fixture and goldens reads to the same values PyYAML gave: the six tags goldens (`tags-apply`, `tags-check`, `tags-index`, `tags-render`, `tags-show`, `tags-unknown-sub`) and both `reindex` goldens replay byte for byte; unit tests in `yaml.rs` pin the YAML 1.1 cases (`no`, `On`, `~`, `0x1F`, `1_000`, `010`, `2026-6-5`) and Python's `str()`/`repr()` of each type.

wps.body:

- **`link`**: the plan and the dry run; `--apply` with a backup first; `--name`, `--all-names` and `--limit`; stop after three failures; write the `.inetloc`.

- **Exit codes** match the engine's (recon section 6).
- Remove these modes from the sidecar's source.

**Criteria**: AC-10.1.

wps.title: pplr's own mail reader
wps.objective: Give pplr its own read-only mail reader, so that `pplr email` and `contact log --email` work with no dependency on Geodica's `mail-recent`. Its JSON output becomes a stable contract that other tools, Gtools among them, can call.
wps.body:
**Why** (hv, 2026-11-02): reading recent mail is generally useful, so pplr should own it rather than depend on a private estate script. Once it is done, Gtools can call pplr for it.

**Where it lives: Rust, not Swift.** Mail.app has no public framework for reading a mailbox. `mail-recent` reads Mail's own SQLite files, `~/Library/Mail/V10/MailData/Envelope Index` and `~/Library/Accounts/Accounts4.sqlite`. Rust reads SQLite read-only with `rusqlite`, the bundled build Cldr already uses for BusyCal's store. Swift would add a second process and nothing more. If WP work finds a reason Swift is needed after all, raise it with vc before building.

**Scope**

- **A `mail` module**:
  - opens both databases read-only and never writes;
  - reads the fields pplr uses: date, account, from, sender address, recipients (To, Cc, Bcc), subject and Message-ID;
  - takes the last N hours, or what is in the inbox now, with `--account`, `--sent` and `--limit`, as `mail-recent index` does;
  - skips junk, trash, deleted, drafts, spam and bin, and messages marked deleted;
  - deduplicates by Message-ID.
- **The private schema**: Mail's Envelope Index schema is Apple's and unversioned, so every query lives in one module. That module checks the tables and columns it needs and refuses by name when they differ, rather than returning wrong rows.
- **Access**: reading needs Full Disk Access for the terminal running pplr. Without it, `pplr email` exits non-zero naming the setting, and doctor shows the same row.
- **`pplr email recent|inbox`**: today's numbered listing and its cache in `PPLR_CACHE_DIR`. `contact log --email N` and `contact log --email <Message-ID>` come off hold and complete WP07.
- **`pplr email --json`**: the stable contract. It is a versioned document carrying `schema` and the fields above. Its exit codes are documented: 0, 1 for no access or a schema mismatch, 2 for usage. This is what Gtools calls.
- **Tests** run against a synthetic SQLite fixture built in the test, holding only the tables and columns the module reads. They never touch a real mail store. One `#[ignore]` test reads the live store on rhadamanth on demand, read-only.
- Delete `bin/pplr_email` and `src/pplr-email/email_list.py`.

**Criteria**: AC-14.1 and AC-14.2.

**Depends on**: WP04 and WP07.

**Not in scope**: changing Gtools. Pointing Gtools at `pplr email --json` is Gtools' own work, done after this WP lands.

criteria.text: No Python: `git ls-files '*.py'` is empty, no committed file runs `python3` or `uv`, and the project's check gate fails on either.

One binary: every command the shell pplr offered (the 30 in recon section 4) is served by the Rust `pplr` with the same arguments and flags, and no `bin/pplr*` script, `lib/engine.sh` or run-time build remains.

Parity: the bats suite passes against the Rust binary: every test on macOS, and on Linux every test that needs no macOS service. A test retired as shell-specific is withdrawn on the record, with its reason.

Byte-identical data: over the synthetic fixture tree, every file the Rust binary writes under PPLR_DATA is byte-identical to the legacy golden, apart from the time-dependent fields listed beside the goldens (WP03). The plan workbook matches by content.

Live read-only parity: on rhadamanth, over the live People tree, the read-only commands print the same output under the legacy code (checked out from history into a scratch worktree) and under the Rust binary. Nothing writes to the live tree.

Install-independence: the binary runs from any directory and any install location, with no PPLR_ROOT, PPLR_BIN_DIR, PPLR_TEMPLATE_DIR or checkout. PPLR_DATA, then PPLR_DIR, names the data. Templates, icons and the README come from the binary, or from the data tree's _pplr/ overrides.
Linux honesty: on Linux, every command that needs a macOS service exits non-zero with a message naming why, and every other command works.
One version, current docs: Cargo.toml is the only version source, and README, usage-rules.md, CHANGELOG and intent/llm/ARCHITECTURE.md describe the Rust binary.

Code and data never mix: no name, marker, email or other content from the People tree is in Pplr's tree or history, tests use synthetic data alone, and a leak check that reads PPLR_DATA at run time fails the pre-commit gate on any match.
The bats runner and CI exit non-zero when any test fails.
No test or runner deletes outside its own temporary directory: an inherited PPLR_TEST_DATA, or any other path from the environment, is never a deletion target.
One setting points the bats suite at either implementation, and the default is the legacy code.
The baseline against the legacy code is recorded on this thread for rhadamanth and both CI runners, with a one-line triage for each failing test.

# ST0001 design: Pplr in Rust

Design record by vc, 2026-11-02, from the recon attached to this thread (`recon.md`), dc's boot findings and cc's survey. It fixes what the port must preserve, how the work is divided, and the rules every work package follows. ST0002 ships the result through Homebrew; the two threads meet at the install layout (section 3.4).

## 1. Rulings (hv, 2026-11-02)

### 3.3 The fallback

- The Rust `pplr` looks its command up in its table. 2. **Goldens from the legacy code (WP03).** A synthetic People tree covers the recon's edge cases: accents, multi-word and double-barrelled surnames, all three meeting-note styles, jpg, jpeg and png pictures, aliases, a vocabulary with `also` and `split`, cadence `roster` and `every`, `contact.yaml`, and a Contacts dump with `home`, `other` and `none` accounts and a card linked across accounts. 3. **Unit tests** in each module, for every pure function: the normalisation rules, the marker, header parsing, the matching tiers, scoring, link conversion, the emitters and the cadence arithmetic. Expected values derive from their inputs: no hand-written counts.
4. **The bats suite against the Rust binary** at every WP boundary, on macOS and Linux. A test that checks bash internals (eg "scripts are executable", "bash 4") is rewritten to check behaviour, or withdrawn on the record with its reason.
5. **Live read-only parity (WP13).** On rhadamanth, with the legacy code checked out from history into a scratch worktree, the read-only commands run over the live People tree under both implementations and their output is compared. Nothing writes to the live tree.

The `dump` mode emits exactly the JSON the test fixtures use. - **Normalisation rules** (all pure): case and diacritic folding; phones as digits with `+`, UK assumed for a leading 0, the trunk 0 dropped after nine named country codes (Italy keeps it), several numbers split on `,;·/`; Gmail addresses folded for dots and `+suffix`; LinkedIn reduced to its slug; a Markdown link read as its text. - **The marker**: `pplr:///`, lower case, accents dropped, every run of other characters one hyphen; the first form (`pplr://B/Bray,%20Martin`) is still recognised; aliases from `.index/aliases` resolve too. - **Exit codes**: 3 for no Contacts access, 4 for `resolve` finding nobody, 2 for usage, 1 for any other failure; `link` and `applyplan` stop after three failed writes. ## 7. Precedent for the port and the release Summarised from Cldr, Ccusage and devbin 0.1.19; ST0002's design carries the release detail. - **House style (Cldr is the newest and canonical; Ccusage ships Python, so it is not a model for tooling):** one crate at the repo root; edition 2024; `rustfmt.toml` with `tab_spaces = 2`; `unsafe_code = "forbid"`, `unwrap_used` and `expect_used` denied; a 9-line `main.rs` calling `cli::run`; `lib.rs` as the module list; a hand-rolled CLI with a `HELP` constant and small `take_value` and `take_flag` helpers (no clap, anyhow or thiserror); `Box` errors that name the file or setting; "pure core, thin shell", with writes through a temp file; each dependency commented with why; unit tests in each module returning `Result`; one integration file, `tests/cli.rs`, with a `Sandbox` that redirects HOME, XDG and PATH (devbin's `check autotests` refuses a second `tests/*.rs`); no hand-written counts in tests. - **`forbid` cannot be relaxed** by an inner `#[allow]`, so framework bindings such as `objc2-contacts` would need the crate lint lowered or a second crate. Ccusage reaches macOS through the safe `security-framework` crate; nothing here uses objc2. - **TCC**: Cldr's Full Disk Access grant lands on the terminal that runs it. A CLI's Contacts grant does the same today ("the app running pplr, eg iTerm or Terminal"), which is why the engine needs no signing. - **Release**: Cldr renders a source-build formula into `matthewsinclair/homebrew-cldr`; Ccusage ships Developer ID signed tarballs (for Keychain access) and builds from source on Linux. devbin 0.1.19's release core and `formula: mode: source` cover what Pplr needs without either project's bespoke tools.
